sections.html:
Springville nestles against the Wasatch Range in Utah County, nearly all of it east of Interstate 15 and roughly 3 miles from Utah Lake's average shoreline. Locals call it Art City, after the Springville Museum of Art, which dates to about 1937. Many residents drive to work in Provo-Orem or Salt Lake City, so freeway access weighs on buyers' minds. Houses near an I-15 exit are easiest to reach, and a seller can point to that.

Property matters go through Provo, where the county assessor, treasurer and recorder have their offices. Nebo School District runs the schools, among them Springville High School, Springville Junior High and Spring Canyon Middle School, with Reagan Academy and Merit Academy as charter options.

Housing measureSpringville, 2020 to 2024
Population, 2020 count35,268
Population, 2010 count29,466
Owner-occupied housing rate71.7%
Median value of owner-occupied homes$454,400
Median gross rent$1,572

Between 2010 and 2020 the population rose 19.7%. Owners occupy about seven in ten homes. Read the median as a survey result and not as an estimate for your own address.

sections.h2: Rental units, ADUs and short-term stays
sections.html:
Renting out part of your house is possible, though the city attaches ownership and occupancy conditions. ADUs belong only in single-family residential zones, so duplexes, twin homes and apartments are out.

  • The owner needs a stake of 50% or more in the property.
  • One of the two units has to be owner-occupied, so the main house and the ADU cannot both be rentals.
  • Interior conversions and detached ADUs both need a building permit.
  • A stay shorter than 30 days counts as short-term and calls for a city business license, with the host living in the main dwelling and on hand.

Leasing the upstairs and downstairs to different tenants turns on the zone, and on whether the second unit was legally permitted or counts as a legal nonconforming use. Never permitted your basement apartment? Say so to the buyer before anyone signs.

A permit is needed ahead of any work that enlarges, repairs, alters, adds to or tears down a structure, or that installs equipment in it. Ask the city's building division which jobs state guidelines exempt.

Expect an inspection within three business days of asking, never the same day. Anything submitted after 5:00 p.m. on Friday, through Sunday night, is treated as received Monday. Call the building office at 801-489-2704. If a project is still open or was never finished, close it out with the city before you sell, because an open permit can slow a closing and make a buyer nervous.

A remodel done without a permit may prompt questions from a buyer's inspector or lender. Request your permit history from the city before listing.

Power, water and public works are all city departments. The Springville Power Department operates the Whitehead Power Plant and has a Customer Generation program that covers solar systems. Call (801) 489-2750 for outages and billing questions.

The culinary water system publishes a yearly water quality report, and recycling is picked up every other week. A buyer moving in will need to set up city utility accounts, so put that on your closing checklist.

Inspections sometimes turn up both. Ten segments make up the Wasatch Fault, and five are active, the Provo segment among them. Forecasters give a 57% chance of a quake of magnitude 6.0 or greater within 50 years.

Elevated radon turns up in one of every three Utah homes, and the action level is 4 picocuries per liter. Run a short test before you list so the result holds no surprise. If the reading is high, you can fix it or sell as is and let the price reflect it.

Springville property is billed by Utah County, and a payment after November 30 draws a penalty. The county Auditor sends a valuation notice every year, and the tax notice itself follows in the second half of October. A home you live in is 45% exempt.

Visit the Treasurer at 100 East Center Street, Suite 1200 in Provo, or phone 801-851-8255. Earlier delinquencies are absent from the bill, so request a payoff figure. Your deed is filed by the Recorder, Suite 1300, 801-851-8179.

Think the value is wrong? The Board of Equalization takes filings until September 15, or 45 days after the notice goes out if that is later. After that the listed value is final for the year. Attach nearby sales and repair estimates.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Springville
sections.html:
Paying cash means no mortgage, no appraisal and no waiting on a loan decision. Describe the house, read the written offer and choose when to close.

Settlement happens at a title or escrow company, and the deed is recorded in Provo. Taxes are split by days of ownership. Mention any unpermitted ADU or addition at the outset. Back taxes are listed by the title company and paid out of what you receive.

Before requesting offers, round up permit records, ADU paperwork, a recent utility bill and your mortgage payoff amount. With an inherited house, either empty it first or tell the buyer what remains and ask if they will accept it that way.

sections.h2: Selling a house with an unpermitted unit
sections.html:
Work done without a permit, such as an apartment or an addition, will not make a house unsellable, but it shapes the talks. Raise it with the buyer early. A mortgage lender may refuse to count a unit missing from the records, and that can sink a financed purchase near the end.

Two routes exist. One is to seek the permit and fix the work before listing, which costs time and money. The other is a cash buyer who accepts the house in its current state and sorts out the legal side later. With a tenant in place, share the lease and rent history, and keep the owner-occupancy rules above in mind when describing what a new owner may do.

1. Give us the address, the condition and your timing.
  2. Read the written offer and ask questions.
  3. Accept it, sign the purchase agreement and a title company opens the file.
  4. Title staff confirm ownership and taxes and draft the closing statement.
  5. You sign, the deed is recorded in Provo and payment follows.

With no loan involved there is no appraisal to wait for, so speed depends on title work and your own calendar.

• A basement apartment lacking a permit or a clear record of owner occupancy.
  • Nightly rentals where the host did not live in the main dwelling.
  • Remodeling finished without a building permit.
  • Possessions left inside an inherited house.

Disclose any that apply. A buyer who hears it from you early rarely walks away later.

faqs.a: Yes. County offices in Provo value the property, send the bill and record deeds, and Nebo School District runs the schools.

faqs.q: When are Springville property taxes due?
faqs.a: Pay by November 30 to avoid a penalty. Notices go out in the second half of October.

faqs.q: Can I have a basement apartment in Springville?
faqs.a: Only as a permitted ADU in a single-family zone, with the owner holding at least 50% and living in one of the two units. A building permit is needed.

faqs.q: How many people live in Springville?
faqs.a: About 35,268 people in 2020, a 19.7% rise over the 29,466 counted in 2010.

faqs.q: Does a Springville short-term rental need a license?
faqs.a: Yes. Stays under 30 days require a city business license, and the host must live in the main dwelling and be present.
